chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performs salat (prayer) in one corner of the room while his wife or his daughter performs salat (prayer) beside him in the other corner. He said: “That is not appropriate; but if there is a handspan between them, it suffices,” meaning when the man is ahead of the woman by a handspan.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it is sufficient or valid for him
key_terms.بِحِذَائِهِ: beside him or parallel to him
key_terms.زَاوِيَةِ: corner or side of a room
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: a handspan as a measure of distance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man and his wife or daughter praying beside each other in the same room?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the relative positioning of a man and a woman during salat (prayer) in the same room. It indicates that praying directly side by side is not appropriate, and that a small forward separation by the man—described as a handspan—is sufficient.
